messages.author: e4abc4cc8b21676e
messages.subject: Shiny | iframe | reactive
parts:
Hello all,
I am trying to display a dynamic iframe to display youtube videos based on user's input for the URL.
My code does not generate error, but the video does not display, would you have any solution ?
Many thanks in advance!
Regards,
Thomas

My code:

ui.R

[...]
box(title = "settings", status = "warning", solidHeader = TRUE, width = 2,
                    textInput("texturli", label = "enter valid Youtube URL", value = "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7mXGMcpA0g"),
                    actionButton("geturl", label = "launch analysis")
                  ),
box(title = "video", status = "primary", solidHeader = TRUE, width = 3,
                    tags$iframe(src = "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7mXGMcpA0g"), # this works fine
                    htmlOutput("test"))                                                                             # this does not work
[...]

server.R

[...]
url <- reactive({
    input$geturl
    isolate(paste0(input$texturli))
  })

  output$test <- renderUI({
    tags$iframe(src = url())
  })
[...]

messages.subject: Re: Shiny | iframe | reactive
parts:
In server.R, try this block instead: 

  output$test <- renderUI({
      e <- '<iframe id="app" src="URL" width="100%"></iframe>'
      HTML(gsub("URL",  url(), e))
  })

renderUI({

})

It is a better solution than constructing the HTML code manually,
especially when the URL contains special HTML entities.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Shiny | iframe | reactive
parts:
Sure. Here is a short example:

> library(shiny)
> tags$iframe(url = 'http://foo.bar.com/?a=1&b=2')
<iframe url="http://foo.bar.com/?a=1&b=2"></iframe>

You see & is escaped to &. Other special characters include ", <,
and >. If you want to construct an HTML tag, normally I'd recommend
you to use tags$ unless you are 100% sure the tag content/attributes
do not contain special characters.

Regards,
Yihui
